profilePeriod: Primarily 2019–2022 premiership; earlier religious context and explicitly dated 2023 accountability finding and 2026 Ukraine update.

sources.title: Levelling Up speech
sources.evidence: Johnson calls Britain overcentralised and proposes flexible English devolution, elected local leadership and private investment.

sources.title: Union of the United Kingdom: Under stress?
sources.evidence: Parliamentary research records Johnson rejecting in January 2020 a transfer of powers for another Scottish independence referendum.

sources.title: Miller / Cherry judgment
sources.evidence: Supreme Court held his advice to prorogue Parliament unlawful because it frustrated parliamentary functions without reasonable justification.

sources.title: Privileges Committee final report
sources.evidence: Committee found deliberate misleading of House and committee, undermining parliamentary process and complicity in intimidation. This is a dated later accountability finding, not a claim Johnson endorsed its conclusions.

sources.title: Beating Crime Plan announcement
sources.evidence: Government expanded electronic monitoring and relaxed stop-and-search conditions; combined enforcement with prevention.

sources.title: Plan B statement
sources.evidence: Johnson required masks and Covid passes in large venues; a negative test remained an alternative to vaccination.

sources.title: Points-based immigration policy statement
sources.evidence: Introduced salary and skills thresholds and intended reduction in lower-skilled immigration.

sources.title: Migration and Rwanda speech
sources.evidence: Promoted Rwanda relocation and controlled borders; simultaneously praised immigrant contributions and legal refuge for Hong Kong, Afghan, Syrian and Ukrainian arrivals.

sources.title: Integrated Review nuclear deterrent
sources.evidence: Raised nuclear stockpile ceiling to 260, while describing deterrence and NATO commitments rather than unlimited aggressive war.

sources.title: Address to Ukrainian Parliament
sources.evidence: Supported Ukrainian resistance with British military aid and condemned Russian invasion.

sources.title: YES annual meeting day two summary
sources.evidence: Event organiser records Johnson on 12 September calling for Western strategic clarity and condemning Russia’s imperial aims against Ukraine.

sources.title: Economy speech in Dudley
sources.evidence: Praised furlough protection and public investment in post-pandemic recovery, alongside enterprise and infrastructure.

sources.title: Health and social care statement
sources.evidence: Defended NHS financed through taxes and announced a health/social-care levy; explicitly acknowledged breaking a no-tax-rise pledge.

sources.title: Greenwich free-trade speech
sources.evidence: Promoted comparative advantage and global free trade while reclaiming regulatory sovereignty, protecting NHS and maintaining labour/environmental standards.

sources.title: Steel safeguard statement
sources.evidence: Johnson government extended safeguards across fifteen steel categories, showing sectoral exceptions to free-trade rhetoric.

sources.title: High Profiles interview, originally Third Way
sources.evidence: Described religion as private, variable faith and mixed family religious heritage; valued spiritual life but declined categorical answers on embryological research.

sources.title: Christmas message
sources.evidence: Celebrated Christ’s birth and religious freedom for persecuted Christians; addressed the wider population inclusively.

sources.title: Pride Month at Downing Street
sources.evidence: Proud of same-sex marriage across UK; met LGBT people and supported inclusion, conversion-therapy ban commitment and restored military medals.

sources.title: Reuters: abortion decision response
sources.evidence: Johnson criticised overturning Roe v Wade and defended women’s choice.

sources.title: ITV: comments on transgender sport
sources.evidence: Supported sex-based female sporting categories and parental involvement in irreversible treatment, alongside sympathy for people transitioning.

sources.title: UN General Assembly technology speech
sources.evidence: Optimistic about AI, regenerative medicine, neural interfaces and genomics, but warned against surveillance, censorship and uncontrolled technological consequences.

sources.title: Ten-point green industrial plan announcement
sources.evidence: Combined nuclear power, innovation, electric transport and nature restoration in a growth-oriented net-zero programme.

sources.title: Genetic technologies regulation response
sources.evidence: Government sought to ease plant gene-editing research restrictions under proportionate scientific regulation.

sources.title: Unleashed publisher catalogue
sources.evidence: Publisher lists Boris Johnson as author of Unleashed, a political memoir covering his elected offices and premiership.

sources.title: HarperCollins Frankfurt rights guide
sources.evidence: Indexed publisher catalogue gives first publication as 10 October 2024; full PDF fetch exceeded web tool size limit.

sources.title: Brazilian coverage of Unleashed
sources.evidence: Brazilian coverage names memoir by original title Unleashed and treats Libertado as literal translation; no Brazilian published translation verified.

facts: 2021: flexible local devolution and metro mayors.
2020: refused new Scottish secession referendum powers.
estrutura.tension: Local administrative empowerment inside a protected Union; neither unrestricted secession nor uniform central administration.

facts: Electoral parliamentary politician; Brexit justified through public mandate.
2019 unlawful prorogation; 2023 parliamentary findings of misleading Parliament.
representacao.tension: Commitment to popular electoral authority coexists with executive pressure on parliamentary oversight; do not erase either.

facts: 2021: expanded stop-and-search and electronic monitoring.
2021: Covid passes with testing alternative.
2019: denounced digital authoritarianism and defended expression/privacy.
poder.tension: Law-and-order government with civil-libertarian rhetoric; neither police-state absolutism nor unrestricted private drug use follows.

facts: 2020: selected migration through skills/salary thresholds.
2022: Rwanda removals alongside praise for lawful migration and refugee routes.
imigracao.tension: National border control does not imply ethnic exclusion or compulsory abandonment of every immigrant custom.

facts: 2021: expanded nuclear ceiling.
2022: armed Ukraine; 2026: continued opposition to Russian imperialism.
diplomacia.tension: Deterrence and allied military support, not pacifism; defence of sovereignty differs from unlimited preventive conquest.

facts: 2020: restored British sovereignty and autonomous external policy.
2022: actively supported Ukraine; September 2026 reiterated need for Western resolve.
intervencao.tension: British national agency and active alliances, not isolationism; sovereign choice also recognised for Ukraine.

facts: 2020: enterprise and free trade with NHS protected.
2021: defended public tax-funded healthcare.
economia.tension: Supports private enterprise without privatising every public function or abolishing the social safety net.

facts: 2020: furlough and public infrastructure recovery.
2021: raised taxes for NHS/social care despite prior pledge.
2020: defended minimum wage and labour standards while rejecting wholesale EU regulatory alignment.
controle.tension: Regulated capitalism and selective intervention; neither comprehensive planning nor consistently minimal taxation.

facts: 2020: explicitly opposed protectionist global trend and sought trade agreements.
2022: maintained steel safeguards.
comercio.tension: Free trade qualified by sovereignty, strategic industry and standards; Brexit is not evidence of economic autarky.

facts: 2004: fluctuating private faith and plural family heritage.
2019: celebrated Christianity and protection against religious persecution.
religiao.tension: Cultural Christian attachment and religious freedom coexist with personal uncertainty and non-theocratic government.

facts: 2021: supported same-sex marriage and LGBT inclusion.
2022: defended abortion choice.
2022: supported sex-based sports categories and parental involvement.
moral.tension: Social liberalism on marriage/abortion does not establish every progressive identity or family-policy position.

facts: 2019: praised medical/neural/genomic innovation while warning against abuses.
2020: nuclear and green industry alongside nature protection.
2021: plant gene-editing liberalisation.
tecnologia.tension: Technological optimism with environmental and ethical boundaries; no verified endorsement of unrestricted human enhancement.

limitations: Profile period preserved verbatim from existing research; earlier answers, vectors and score reports were not consulted.
Research checked through 2026-10-01; newest verified substantive statement used is 2026-09-12. Later Ukraine statements confirm continuity; not all domestic positions were restated in 2026.
Government speeches evidence stated priorities, not successful implementation; court, Parliament, independent interviews and reporting provide cross-checks.
Brazil-specific questions are translated by functional analogy into UK policy; no invented view on Brazilian constitutional particulars.
Questions on embryo enhancement, polyamory, racial quotas and cryptocurrency require cautious inference from documented principles; absence of a statement alone is not neutral.

No verified Brazilian translation of Unleashed found after title/author/translation searches; use original title, not an invented literal Portuguese title. Publisher PDF date was available in search extract, while full fetch failed due to size.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political memoir directly covering his premiership and political ideas; more directly relevant to this profile than his Churchill biography. No existing books.json entry; no verified Brazilian translation.

neutralReasons.estrutura_19: Local accountability versus national standards and central support: neither sole municipal administration nor entirely national delivery captures devolution policy.
neutralReasons.estrutura_11: Community autonomy within a common national legal framework pulls in both directions in this UK analogy.
neutralReasons.representacao_05: Constitutional review and parliamentary-majority sovereignty conflict, illustrated by prorogation litigation.
neutralReasons.poder_12: Individual autonomy conflicts with protective legal/clinical boundaries; not treated as a categorical euthanasia campaign position.
neutralReasons.imigracao_05: Integration and civic obligations are demanded, but lawful foreign cultural practices are welcomed; the broad word customs straddles these.
neutralReasons.diplomacia_06: He promotes diplomatic work and arsenal expansion together rather than accepting a blanket priority hierarchy.
neutralReasons.economia_09: Tax-funded NHS and public education coexist with commercial utilities; the bundled statement produces real mixed commitment.
neutralReasons.controle_08: Minimum-wage support and employment competitiveness both matter, making the unspecified too-high threshold indeterminate.
neutralReasons.controle_12: Financial innovation is welcome but replacing monetary authority with unrestricted competing currencies conflicts with regulated capitalism.
neutralReasons.comercio_08: Global exchange is a positive aim but borderless economic governance conflicts with sovereignty and strategic safeguards.
neutralReasons.religiao_02: Private and fluctuating faith has cultural influence without controlling all moral or political decisions.
neutralReasons.religiao_14: Religious wedding tradition is valued but civil and same-sex marriage are also accepted.
neutralReasons.moral_12: Parental involvement and universal education both have legitimate roles.
neutralReasons.moral_02: Traditional family affection coexists with equal recognition for other family forms.
neutralReasons.tecnologia_04: Innovation in the body is positive but ethical and safety limits matter; statement bundles restriction and prohibition.
neutralReasons.tecnologia_08: Nature restoration and industrial acceleration were joint goals of the green industrial programme.
neutralReasons.tecnologia_09: Medical genetic treatment and elective intelligence enhancement are distinct; genuine documented embryological caution conflicts with genomic enthusiasm.
